issuing_body: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
title: Four Men Plead Guilty to $2M Minnesota Medicaid Fraud
supports: Moktar Hassan Aden, Mustafa Dayib Ali, Khalid Ahmed Dayib, and Abdifitah Mohamud Mohamed each pleaded guilty to one count of wire fraud in separate hearings between 2026-07-07 and 2026-07-23.
DOJ states the four used Brilliant Minds Services LLC to enroll about 350 HSS recipients and fraudulently obtain approximately $2.2 million from Minnesota Medicaid between April 2022 and April 2025.
DOJ states the defendants fabricated supporting records using ChatGPT after insurers questioned their claims.
Sentences had not yet been set as of the release.

money.notes: DOJ's post-plea release says the defendants fraudulently obtained approximately $2.2 million. Treat guilt as adjudicated, but do not upgrade this press-release figure to restitution_ordered, recovered_amount, or a judgment-certified proven_loss without the plea agreements or judgments. It overlaps the earlier approximately $2.3 million amount_billed allegation.

does_not_support: No sentence, restitution order, forfeiture order, or collected-recovery amount is stated in this release.
The $2.2 million post-plea government characterization overlaps the earlier Brilliant Minds billing allegation and must not be summed with it.
